Don't show this message again Close Print Government debt at 87.7% and 81.5% respectively Overview In the euro area (EA20) the government deficit to GDP ratio remained unchanged at 3.0% in 2024 and 2025. In the EU , it also remained unchanged at 3.1%, the same level as in 2024. In the euro area the government debt to GDP ratio increased from 86.6% at the end of 2024 to 87.7% at the end of 2025, and in the EU from 80.3% to 81.5%. In this release, Eurostat, the statistical office of the European Union , is providing government deficit and debt data for the years 2022-2025, based on figures reported by EU Member States in the second notification in 2026, for the application of the excessive deficit procedure (EDP). This notification is based on the ESA 2010 system of national accounts. This release also includes data on government expenditure and revenue. Don't show this message again Close Print 82.9% of GDP in EU Overview At the end of the second quarter of 2026, the general government gross debt to GDP ratio in the euro area (EA21) stood at 88.8%, an increase compared with 88.4% at the end of the first quarter of 2026. In the EU , the ratio also increased from 82.5% to 82.9%. Compared with the second quarter of 2025, the government debt to GDP ratio increased in both the euro area (from 87.3% to 88.8%) and the EU (from 81.4% to 82.9%). At the end of the second quarter of 2026, the general government debt was made up of 84.5% debt securities in the euro area and 83.9% in the EU , 13.1% loans in the euro area and 13.8% in the EU and 2.4% currency and deposits in both the euro area and the EU . Due to the involvement of EU Member States' governments in lending to certain Member States, quarterly data on intergovernmental lending (IGL) are also published. The IGL as percentage of GDP at the end of the second quarter of 2026 stood at 1.3% in the euro area and at 1.1% in the EU . These data are released by Eurostat, the statistical office of the European Union . Don't show this message again Close Print Up by 1.4% in the euro area and by 2.6% in the EU compared with August 2025 Overview In August 2026, compared with July 2026, seasonally adjusted production in construction increased by 1.8% in the euro area and by 2.0% in the EU , according to first estimates from Eurostat, the statistical office of the European Union . In July 2026, production in construction grew by 0.2% in the euro area and fell by 0.1% in the EU . In August 2026, compared with August 2025, production in construction increased by 1.4% in the euro area and by 2.6% in the EU . Monthly comparison by construction sector and by Member State In the euro area in August 2026, compared with July 2026, production in construction decreased by 0.4% for construction of buildings, decreased by 2.1% for civil engineering, increased by 2.5% for specialised construction activities. In the EU , production in construction decreased by 1.0% for construction of buildings, decreased by 0.2% for civil engineering, increased by 2.3% for specialised construction activities. Among Member States for which data are available, the highest monthly increases in production in construction were recorded in Hungary (+14.0%), Germany (+9.3%) and Romania (+7.2%). The largest decreases were observed in Slovenia (-5.1%), Slovakia (-4.9%) and Italy (-2.9%).
